prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
competitors_mentioned: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a short list of reputable HVAC companies that serve Houston and explain why to call each — and then a quick checklist of what to ask and how to pick. If you tell me your ZIP code and a few details (central AC vs. heat pump vs. ductless, symptoms, unit age, any warranty) I can customize the list for your neighborhood.

Top Houston HVAC companies to call (and why)

1. John Moore Services
- Why call: Houston-based, large local company with long experience in HVAC, plumbing and home services; offers 24/7 emergency service, preventative maintenance plans, and factory-authorized service for many brands. Well-known locally for same-day repairs and parts availability.

2. ARS/Rescue Rooter (often listed as ARS)
- Why call: National chain with a big Houston footprint, multiple service trucks (so faster arrival), techs trained and often NATE-certified, and availability for emergency repairs. Good for quick diagnostics and immediate repairs.

3. Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning
- Why call: National/large regional presence with authorized dealer status for many major brands; they typically offer diagnostics, warranties on repairs, maintenance agreements, and trained technicians. Good if you want a brand-authorized service.

4. One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (and/or Benjamin Franklin Heating & Air — same parent company in many markets)
- Why call: Franchise with a service-punctuality reputation (on-time promise), flat-rate pricing options, and standardized service procedures. Useful if you want predictable pricing and fast response.

5. Local independent NATE-certified shops (examples: look for “HVAC Solutions,” “A/C Repairs Houston,” etc., in your ZIP)
- Why call: Independent shops often have lower labor rates, techs with deep local experience, and more flexible scheduling. Many independents are NATE-certified and carry extended labor warranties. Use local review sites to find the best-rated independent in your neighborhood.

Why I’m recommending these types rather than only a single name
- Manufacturer-authorized dealers and larger chains often have brand-specific training, parts, and warranties.
- Independent local shops can be quicker and less expensive for routine repairs.
- Calling multiple options (one large company, one authorized dealer if you have a brand warranty, and one well-reviewed local shop) gives you price and service comparisons.

What to check before you agree to a repair
- Confirm they are registered with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) and ask for their HVAC contractor registration number.
- Ask if techs are NATE-certified and EPA 608 certified (required for refrigerant work).
- Ask about a diagnostic fee, whether it’s waived with repair, cost of common parts (capacitor, contactor, motor), labor warranty, and parts warranty.
- Get a written estimate before work begins and insist they document the cause of the failure.
- If your unit is under manufacturer warranty, call the manufacturer first to verify authorized service providers to avoid voiding warranty.

What to tell them on the phone (have this info ready)
- Your ZIP code and address (or neighborhood)
- Make/model and age of the outdoor A/C unit if you know it
- Symptoms (not cooling, short-cycling, leaking water, odd noises, tripping breaker, smell)
- When the problem started and whether you’ve had recent repairs or maintenance

Quick pricing expectations (ballpark)
- Diagnostic visit: often $75–$150 (may be waived if you proceed with repair)
- Common part repairs (capacitor, contactor, sensor): typically a few hundred dollars
- Compressor or major refrigerant/coil work: can be $1,000–$3,500+ depending on unit and refrigerant
(Exact pricing varies; get written quotes from at least two companies.)

Next step
- Tell me your ZIP code and a brief description of the problem and the AC type, and I’ll prioritize the best local options (and can draft a short phone script you can use when you call).
